title: What Tokens are Learned when Tokenization is Optimized Jointly with Language Modeling?
abstract: arXiv:2608.17325v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Tokenization is a fundamental component of language modeling pipelines. Despite its importance, it is often fixed, even though it significantly impacts model performance across languages. In this work, we analyze what tokens are learned when tokenization is jointly optimized with language modeling. We compare tokenizer-free approaches such as SSLMs and H-Nets with fixed tokenizers across 18 typologically and script-diverse languages. Our results show that joint optimization fundamentally alters token structure. SSLMs recover morphologically aligned and contextually efficient tokens, whereas H-Nets prioritize byte-level efficiency, producing longer tokens with very low overlap with standard subword vocabularies. We further show that tokenization behavior varies across language typologies. Agglutinative languages exhibit more dynamic segmentation patterns while learning. translated_title: 当分词与语言建模联合优化时，学到了什么词元？
translated_abstract: 分词是语言建模流程中的基础组件。尽管其重要性不言而喻，但它通常是固定的，即便它显著影响模型在多种语言上的性能。在本研究中，我们分析了当分词与语言建模联合优化时，学到了哪些词元。我们将无分词器方法（如SSLMs和H-Nets）与固定分词器在18种类型学和文字多样性语言上进行了比较。结果表明，联合优化从根本上改变了词元结构。SSLMs恢复了形态对齐且上下文高效的词元，而H-Nets优先考虑字节级效率，产生更长的词元，与标准子词词汇的重叠度极低。我们进一步表明，分词行为因语言类型而异。黏着语在训练过程中表现出更动态的切分模式。通过下游评估，使用预训练后微调的BERT模型...
tldr: 本文发现，将分词与语言建模联合优化会改变词元学习方式，其中SSLMs生成形态对齐的词元，而H-Nets偏向字节效率，且不同语言类型（如黏着语）表现出更动态的切分行为。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that jointly optimizing tokenization with language modeling alters token learning, with SSLMs yielding morphologically aligned tokens and H-Nets favoring byte efficiency, while agglutinative languages show more dynamic segmentation patterns.
